head: Fitbit Air notifications: Cuff app makes the band buzz for calls
dek: The Fitbit Air has a vibration motor, but Google only uses it for silent alarms. Cuff, an Android app built by a Reddit user, connects to the band over Bluetooth and makes it vibrate for calls, chosen contacts and apps like Slack and Telegram.
details: You pick which apps and contacts get through and set a vibration pattern and strength for each, so a message from family can feel different from a work chat. The band still doesn't show or read the notification; it only buzzes. Cuff also has a health section that tracks sleep debt over the week and can save meals you eat often. It's a community project, not from Google, and Android Police says installing it may set off a Google Play Protect warning.
where: Android phones with a Fitbit Air; installed from outside Google Play
means: If you missed calls because your Fitbit Air stayed silent, Cuff can fix that, but it's an unofficial app from one person, not from Google.
todo: Only install it if you're fine with a sideloaded app and the Play Protect warning. Keep the list of apps short, or the band will buzz all day.
